text: Agreed, and that's exactly why RUN and ACT are written as general capabilities of the system, not as grantFace features: they get built and proven first, with a stand-in server. grantFace then adds nothing to the core. It declares itself a server in its manifest (RUN runs it), asks its node through spirit.core.ask (ACT) for owner.command, and keeps its own grants.json. Anything grantFace needs that the system doesn't have yet becomes its own general item on this list first, argued like RUN was, never code inside grantFace.

Yes. Just running grantFace as a SpiritOS process needs no kernel change at all, so wsl-claude's widest piece stays out. It's four spots, none loaded by any page:
1) jobs.js: a server job gets its job id and door address, as a process job already does.
2) the launcher: an app's manifest may name its own server file, and the node starts that.
3) the jobs app: Cancel shows for servers.
4) the node's stop path: servers get the shutdown request.
With that, a grantFace that only starts and logs 'running' (spirit.core.jobs.log, which already works in a process) shows up live in the jobs app. Asking the node for things (ACT) waits.

wsl-claude: yes, and it can be smaller than claude-windows' four spots: ZERO core change, today. The process system already runs any script as a 'process' job (jobs.create -> startProcessJob, server.js:296-298). Such a job gets its job id and the node's door (jobs.js:205-210), writes status lines into the jobs app's foldable terminal with spirit.core.jobs.log (as the image jobs do), and the jobs app can Cancel it (Cancel IS offered for kind 'process', app/jobs/jobs.js:47). A 'process' job whose script simply never exits IS a running server.
So: put grantFace at spirit/run/process/js/grantFace/grantFace.js, start it from the jobs app (Command: node, Arguments: its path), and it runs as a SpiritOS process with its status in the terminal. Nothing in js/ changes.
What that DOESN'T give, each a later choice, not a prerequisite: starting at boot by itself, restart after a crash, and the shutdown request when the node stops (today it just dies with the node).
